newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end higher on Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end higher on Iraq news.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices ended higher Thursday on a report that U.N. oil monitors were arrested by a Kurdish faction in northern Iraq, although U.N. officials in Iraq said they had no knowledge of the arrests.

Talk that there was a fire or some other disruption at an Exxon oil refinery in the U.S. Gulf sharpened gasoline's gains, said dealers. But, Exxon said both its refineries in the region were operating normally.
June crude ended 30 cents a barrel higher at $20.03, while May gasoline ended 1.10 cents a gallon higher at 62.84 cents.
May heating oil finished up 0.24 cent at 55.89 cents a gallon. Traders the price pop not a strong enough jolt to oil prices on a bullish footing longer term.
"The news certainly helped propel us today, but I think we will still trade sideways," said Andy Lebow, trader with E. D. & F. Man International in New York.
U.N. officials in Baghdad have no knowledge of United Nations oil monitors being arrested in northern Iraq, as reported Thursday by the BBC monitoring service.

The BBC report, quoting the Iraqi Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) radio said six U.N. envoys monitoring the distribution of fuel in northern Iraq disappeared this week in areas under the control of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
Last August, the KDP joined with troops of Iraq's President Saddam Hussein in battles against the PUK in northern Iraq.
The conflict detained the implementation of the oil-for-food deal between the U.N. and Iraq.

Under the deal, which ended up getting final approval in December, U.N. eased sanctions against Iraq allowing Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months on a renewable basis in exchange for food and other humanitarian aid.
Dealers were concerned that if the arrests were confirmed by the United Nations, the United Nations would consider not renewing the accord for the second six month period which would begin in June.
Still, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said earlier this month in Geneva that he expected the U.N. Security Council to renew the deal.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
